items.description: JenkinsPipelineUtils: a real Groovy parse gate — "a `.kubecoder/project.yaml` for JenkinsPipelineUtils whose test entry point parses every `vars/*.groovy`, which turns the estate-wide failure mode into a pre-push gate". `kc project test` in the repo is green and compiles every `vars/*.groovy` through the pipeline engine's CPS transform on Groovy 2.4.21, its libraries resolved by Maven on the Java toolchain (today the repo has no `.kubecoder/` and seven `vars/*.groovy` files).
The gate can fail: a syntax error in any `vars/*.groovy` turns it red, and so does a construct the CPS transform refuses at load time (e.g. a `synchronized` block). Both reds are witnessed.
"Every" holds going forward: a file added to `vars/` is compiled by the gate without the gate being edited.
The gate changes nothing Jenkins loads: none of its files sit under `src/`, `vars/` or `resources/`, and its build output is not tracked by git.

The IaC/ArgoCDTools job no longer publishes images without running the suite: it runs both images' suites — the same commands as the repo's local test verb — in the iac toolchain image, before either image build (today `Jenkinsfile:16-56` has only the clone and the two kaniko stages).

The consequence "A commit that reds the repo's tests still publishes to registry:5000 on a push to main" no longer holds: a red suite ends the build before either kaniko stage, so neither `argocd-hook` nor `aac-tools` is published from it.
The first IaC/ArgoCDTools run after the push is green, and its log shows both suites running in the iac toolchain container before the image builds.

JenkinsPipelineUtils' `containerTemplates` offers the iac toolchain image (`registry:5000/kube-coder-iac-toolchain`) as a sidecar template, and the ArgoCDTools job takes its test container from it (today `vars/containerTemplates.groovy:12-76` has no kube-coder-* toolchain entry).

promtool in the iac toolchain so alert rules are unit-tested: PrometheusDeploy's local test verb runs `promtool check rules` with the iac toolchain's promtool, pinned to prd's Prometheus 3.14.0 (DockerImages `kube-coder-iac-toolchain/Dockerfile:19,116-122`), over the alerting rules as the chart renders them from `config/prd/values.yaml` (`:58-298`). There is no Jenkins stage.

promtool unit tests cover every alert in the rendered rules file, each with a firing case and a quiet case, and the memory-pressure group carries the scenarios slice 018 witnessed. The test verb runs them.

Neither consequence holds any longer. "A PromQL precedence or matching mistake in an alert rule passes the gate": a unit test catches it. "The prd Prometheus rejects the reloaded rules file" on a syntax or template error: the check catches it. Both reds are witnessed.
The rule tests are self-contained. They feed synthetic series and assert the rules' own thresholds and windows, and none depends on another repo's CronJob schedule or deadline.

argo-cd D61 (`argo-cd/decisions.md:759-773`) no longer gives "deploy repos run no tests" as a standing reason. It records that deploy repos run no tests in Jenkins and that PrometheusDeploy's local test verb checks and unit-tests its alert rules. The retirement of HelmCharts' alert tests and grafana's Keycloak login test is still justified.

Retire modern-app-dev and modern-app-dev-playwright: carried by slice 030 per the D1 ruling. This slice leaves the `modern_app_dev` template (`vars/containerTemplates.groovy:74-76`) and both images in place, so no pipeline loses a template it resolves.
